answer: Random Challenge Execution Window Agents register by crossing a cryptographic bridge tied to a time-locked block hash. When tasks arrive, a decentralized beacon broadcasts an unpredictable seed resembling shifting tides across a deep digital ocean. Each identity must immediately compute a unique cryptographic puzzle using this live seed. Sybil attackers controlling thousands of nodes cannot precompute solutions before the window closes. Genuine agents succeed cheaply, while attackers face extreme CPU costs and must buy costly yarrow extraction licenses to offset hardware exhaustion.
